ranking_by: bite force in pounds per square inch (psi), measured or modeled
title: The 5 Strongest Animal Bites, Ranked (#1 Isn't on Land)

scenes.text: Lions and tigers don't make this list. Number one isn't a land animal.

scenes.label: Jaguar · 1,500 psi
scenes.text: Number five: the jaguar. Around fifteen hundred psi, stronger than a tiger's bite or a lion's.

scenes.label: Hippo · 1,800 psi
scenes.text: Number four: the hippopotamus. About eighteen hundred psi, and it eats plants.

scenes.label: Alligator · 2,100 psi
scenes.text: Number three: the American alligator. About twenty-one hundred psi, more than the hippo.

scenes.label: Saltwater croc · 3,700 psi
scenes.text: Number two: the saltwater crocodile. Researchers measured about thirty-seven hundred psi in a live one.

scenes.label: Great white · 4,000 psi
scenes.text: Number one: the great white shark. Models of a huge twenty-one footer suggest about four thousand psi.

description:
The five strongest animal bites, ranked by bite force in pounds per square inch.
Number one is a modeled figure for a huge 21-foot great white, so treat it as an estimate.
Which animal would you put at number one?
first_comment: Did the shark surprise you? Which animal should we rank next?
